title: How many acres and square metres is a 2 hectare field?
description: A field is two hectares, and one hectare is two point four seven one acres and ten thousand square metres. Multiplying by two gives the area in acres and in square metres, and dividing back checks each answer. Keeko doubts that the number can stay the same.
teaching_notes: One idea: a conversion fact for one unit is multiplied by the amount. Watch for students who keep the same number and only change the unit name.

source: A field is 2 hectares. How many acres is it? How many square
video_script.why: The child converts an area from hectares to acres and to square metres by multiplying the conversion fact for one unit.
video_script.substitution: Write what one hectare equals in the new unit, then multiply by the number of hectares.
video_script.anchor: a field marked out in a village, two hectares in all, with a signboard showing 2 hectares
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko keeps the number two and only changes the unit name to acres. But one hectare is more than two acres, so two hectares must be more than four acres.
video_script.payoff_line: the field is four point nine four two acres, or twenty thousand square metres

final_answer.spoken: four point nine four two acres, which is twenty thousand square metres

maths_rules: 1 hectare = 10000 square metres; 2 x 10000 = 20000 square metres
Keeko: 2 hectares is not 2 acres; 1 hectare is more than 2 acres, so 2 hectares is more than 4 acres
video_script.design: One idea: the conversion fact for one hectare, times the number of hectares. Wrong idea: keep the number and only change the unit. The field and its signboard stay in the anchor band and the working goes on the board.
open_questions: The worklist field of 2 hectares is a worked example from the migration and is not printed in the book text.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the field in acres and in square metres.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step one, two hectares is two groups of one hectare.
<bookmark mark='acres'/>Each group is two point four seven one acres.
Multiply two by two point four seven one to get four point nine four two acres.
<bookmark mark='each'/>Step two, each hectare is ten thousand square metres.
<bookmark mark='metres'/>Two times ten thousand is twenty thousand square metres.

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, put the answers back in the question.
<bookmark mark='acres'/>Divide four point nine four two by two point four seven one and we get two hectares.
<bookmark mark='metres'/>Divide twenty thousand by ten thousand and we also get two hectares.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The field is four point nine four two acres, or twenty thousand square metres.

<bookmark mark='unit'/>When the unit changes, the number changes too.
